title: Negative information questions with plural olla forms
focus: With plural persons, use me emme ole, te ette ole and he eivät ole after the question word: Miksi te ette ole kotona? Miksi te ette ole kotona? — Koska olemme koulussa.
targetSkills: Negative information questions with plural olla forms
prerequisiteSkills: Negative information questions with singular olla forms

exercises.prompt: Choose the question meaning “Why aren't you at home?”  Address a group (te).
exercises.explanation: Plural means more than one in this grammatical pattern. With plural persons, use me emme ole, te ette ole and he eivät ole after the question word: Miksi te ette ole kotona? (“Why aren't you at home?” addressed to a group). Ole stays unchanged. The complete question means “Why aren't you at home”.

exercises.prompt: Answer “Missä te ette ole?”: choose “We are not at school.”
exercises.explanation: Plural means more than one in this grammatical pattern. An addressed group replies with emme ole (“we are not”) when the reply is negative. An affirmative information answer still uses its ordinary affirmative verb: Olemme koulussa (“We are at school”). He refers to another group and keeps eivät ole in a negative reply about that group. The complete reply means “We are not at school”.
